name: Hsü Ling
bio: Hsü Ling (AD 507–583) is represented here by “The Waters of Lung-t’ou,” a poem of the north-west frontier and the long road home to the capital.
The poems here are Arthur Waley’s version in A Hundred and Seventy Chinese Poems (1918), given with the poet’s name as spelled in those books.

poems.title: The Waters of Lung-t’ou
poems.author: Hsü Ling
poems.collection: A Hundred and Seventy Chinese Poems (1918)
poems.text:
The road that I came by mounts eight thousand feet:
The river that I crossed hangs a hundred fathoms.
The brambles so thick that in summer one cannot pass!
The snow so high that in winter one cannot climb!
With branches that interlace Lung Valley is dark:
Against cliffs that tower one’s voice beats and echoes.
I turn my head, and it seems only a dream
That I ever lived in the streets of Hsien-yang.
